articles.title: Josean Querejeta se plantea dejar la presidencia del Baskonia
articles.standfirst: La pitada ante el Real Madrid en el Buesa Arena, la gota que colma el vaso
articles.summary: La pitada ante el Real Madrid en el Buesa Arena, la gota que colma el vaso
articles.body: En el Kosner Baskonia hay un antes y un después del partido de la Euroliga de la pasada semana ante el Real Madrid. Ese día, Josean Querejeta fue el objetivo de una tremenda pitada por parte de la afición vitoriana, que se ensañó con él al principio, durante y al final del partido. No es la primera vez que hay pitos en el Buesa, pero sí es muy poco habitual que estos estén dirigidos hacia la persona que dirige el club desde hace casi cuatro décadas. Esos pitos, esa muestra total de falta de confianza por parte de la fiel afición del Baskonia, ha sido la gota que colma el vaso, o quizá el telón que cae al final de la función. Josean Querejeta vive sus momentos más duros anímicamente desde que está al frente del Baskonia. Y por eso, tras la pitada que casi fue un plebiscito, el presidente está pensando en dejar la presidencia del club. Si esto se produce, la noticia tendría un impacto brutal por lo que significa la figura de Querejeta en Vitoria y en el baloncesto español. El mandatario del Kosner Baskonia, un mago capaz de reinventarse cada año a pesar de vender a sus jugadores más importantes, no ha podido lidiar con la crisis que se ha desatado en el banquillo del equipo, el verdadero epicentro del terremoto que ahora hay en el club. En una complicada decisión, Querejeta despidió a Paolo Galbiati, ganador de la última Copa del Rey en Valencia y que tenía una conexión muy especial con la grada. En su lugar llegó Velimir Perasovic, en su cuarta etapa en el equipo. Las derrotas han seguido llegando, cinco consecutivas para el croata, dos en Liga Endesa y tres en la Euroliga, donde el equipo es colista (1-7). Y lo peor es el desencanto de los aficionados que, en otras crisis, nunca fallaban. Ante el Madrid en la Euroliga no se llegó a los 10.000 espectadores en el Buesa, algo casi insólito. Hubo pitos, pañolada y hasta mensajes contra la directiva ("Sin rumbo ni planificación deportiva, el Araba se vacía"), se podía leer en una pancarta. Querejeta llegó a la presidencia del Baskonia un 27 de octubre de 1988, hace ahora 38 años. Y entre otras cosas, ha logrado colocar al club en la élite de Europa, convirtiéndose en uno de los 13 socios fundadores de la Euroliga (disputando una final), y hacia malabares cada año cuando tenía que vender jugadores o estos se marchaban a otros equipos, y recomponer una plantilla que siempre ha sido competitiva en todos los frentes. Lo que el Baskonia ha sido en todos los años de su gestión es casi un milagro, pensando en que Vitoria es una ciudad de tan sólo 260.000 y tiene que pelear con mastodontes que cuadriplican su presupuesto Pero además el momento del club era crucial pues había hecho una oferta de compra del Buesa Arena a la Diputación Foral de Navarra para convertir ese espacio en una instalación de primer nivel con una inversión de 153 millones. Si Querejeta deja la presidencia, será un proyecto que puede quedar paralizado y quien sabe si anulado.

articles.title: Mark Tatum Gives An Update On NBA Europe’s Plans For 2027
articles.summary: Since its early 2025 announcement, NBA Europe has grown despite recent challenges. While the EuroLeague's rejection of partnering with both the NBA and FIBA...
articles.body:
Since its early 2025 announcement, NBA Europe has grown despite recent challenges. While the EuroLeague's rejection of partnering with both the NBA and FIBA on the project led some to believe that the project may be pushed back a year, all the way to 2028, with a qualifying competition planned for 2027, recent comments by the NBA's deputy commissioner, Mark Tatum, have suggested otherwise.

NBA Europe will be a 16-team league with 12 permanent teams; FIBA's Basketball Champions League or other domestic competitions could determine the remaining four rotational teams.

The league has attracted significant attention from potential ownership groups led by people with deep ties to the NBA. These include BC Roma, owned by Luka Doncic ; Tony Parker's ASVEL squad ; and the Buss brothers , who formerly owned the Lakers.

So, between the billion-dollar bids, rejection from the EuroLeague, and a stated deadline of just a year from now, where does NBA Europe currently stand?

The NBA's earlier offer to merge with the EuroLeague was rejected by Europe's premier basketball competition as 'colonialist' and 'unacceptable'. Despite this rejection, deputy commissioner Tatum remains 'hopeful' of resolving the matter.

"I don't want to disclose any private conversations with the EuroLeague," Tatum recently said. As we've said before, we continue to be hopeful that we'll reach an agreement, but we're prepared to proceed regardless."

Tatum's answer was much less definite about when NBA Europe would launch. At the same time, the deputy commissioner reiterated that the NBA still planned to launch the league by October 2027, but made no promises.

"Well, we're not stopping," Tatum previously stated. "We're moving and proceeding as quickly as we can. As we just discussed, owe planto begin rolling out the [NBA Europe] project in October of 2027, which is a year from now. So we've got a lot of work to do, but we're moving quickly, and we're not slowing down at all."

One of the reasons the NBA's proposal was rejected was its condition that the EuroLeague's composition could not change, meaning the EuroLeague could not expand or alter the number of shareholder teams.

This condition would have prevented the EuroLeague from expanding to a potential 24 teams from the current 20, as well as from increasing the number of shareholder teams. It has been suggested that the NBA is unlikely to proceed with the sale of its own NBA Europe franchises, some of which have attracted billion-dollar bids, until an agreement of sorts is reached with the EuroLeague.

The EuroLeague has announced that it will expand in two windows, with the first in 2027 and the second in 2031.

Five executives representing major European sports clubs, including Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, Barcelona, AC Milan and Paris Saint-Germain, met with NBA Europe officials in London on Wednesday, per Mark Kleinman of SkyNews . The first three clubs are existing EuroLeague teams. Details of the meeting have not been released publicly.

This meeting in London could help move talks with the EuroLeague forward for two main reasons: First, the NBA has not yet officially moved its launch date for NBA Europe from the fall of 2027. Secondly, a partnership would greatly benefit the NBA, given the EuroLeague's nearly seven decades of experience in the European market.

"We believe that the timing is realistic here. Remember, this is not just about a season," said Tatum, referring to the NBA's set launch date of October 2027 .

Despite being about a year away from the league's launch, many details of the project have not yet been publicly revealed. This includes who the favorites are among the ownership groups that have made multi-million-dollar bids, with all locations receiving bids exceeding $500 million, and some even exceeding $1 billion.

This is not helped by Tatum's statement that the NBA has no specific timeline for announcing the winning bidders.

"There is no timeline yet on when we announce the clubs." Tatum reiterated . "I will say, as I said, our timeline is that we plan to start rolling this thing out a year from now. So in the not-too-distant future, we expect to be able to announce some of the franchises."

While they were part of the meeting in Como, Italy, that rejected the NBA's initial proposal, the NBA's meeting with some of Europe's biggest sports clubs could significantly alter the venture. The NBA could woo PSG and AC Milan to join its Europe venture, a huge win for the league.

On the other hand, the meeting also allows the NBA to approach EuroLeague clubs with a brand-new proposal that may offer more favorable terms for the EuroLeague, now that it is clear the league intends to commit to expansion fully.

As things stand now among the NBA , FIBA, and the EuroLeague, with the stage set for a showdown between basketball powerhouses, it is not yet clear which will emerge victorious.

articles.title: What Memphis basketball proved in preseason and setting the stage for 2026-27
articles.summary: There are no more exhibition games for Memphis basketball in 2026-27. From now on, everything counts.
articles.body:
There are no more exhibition games for Memphis basketball in 2026-27.

On this episode of the Tiger Basketball Podcast, Jason Munz and Jonah Dylan sift through all of the many layers of the Nemanja Popović eligibility ruling and its implications. The specifics of the ruling, what we know about the NCAA's rationale, how Penny Hardaway plans to account for his absence, and why it matters as much as it does.

Also, Munz and Dylan revisit the Tigers' exhibition loss at Arkansas, highlight which players proved the most during the preseason, and get into how much pressure the program is facing as it gets set for the season opener against Iowa State.

articles.title: How to watch Sixers vs. Knicks NBA Cup? Date, time, venue, streaming, TV schedule, injury report and more
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers play their NBA Cup game on Friday night, and the opponent is a team they just beat.
articles.body: The Philadelphia 76ers play their NBA Cup game on Friday night, and the opponent is a team they just beat. The New York Knicks visit Xfinity Mobile Arena for the opener of East Group B. Philadelphia won the first meeting 106-100 on opening night, and the defending champions have had a rough stretch since.Tyrese Maxey and LeBron James lead a Sixers team that is 4-1. Jalen Brunson is carrying a Knicks team that is 2-3 and has lost several close games. A second win would put Philadelphia 2-0 in the season series and give it an early edge in a group that also has the Cavaliers, Heat and Pacers. Both teams arrive with Cup history, since Brunson was the tournament MVP last season and James won the first one in 2023. Tip-off is set for 7:30 p.m. ET, and the game is streaming only.Sixers vs. Knicks NBA Cup PreviewPhiladelphia has the better record and the steadier start. The Sixers beat a shorthanded Indiana Pacers team in their last game, and their only loss this season came against the Detroit Pistons. The offense has come and gone in stretches. It works well in the half court, but the team keeps leaning on defense for easy baskets in transition. Jaylen Brown is averaging 20.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 4.2 assists on good efficiency. James has not had a big scoring night yet, and the stars are still sorting out when to attack and when to defer.New York opened 0-3 and has climbed to 2-3. Mikal Bridges is averaging 5.0 points on 27% shooting, and the team has paused extension talks with Josh Hart and Karl-Anthony Towns. Brunson has found his groove lately, but the Knicks guard has had to carry a heavy load while the noise around the team grows.Two matchups stand out. Joel Embiid and Towns meet again, and Embiid is coming off a double-double and a triple-double. New York also has plenty of wings to throw at Brown and James, so how the Sixers handle that length will decide a lot. A win guarantees Philadelphia no worse than a tie in the season series, which could matter for division standing in the spring. The Knicks swept the Sixers in the playoffs, too.The NBA Cup is in its fourth year, and all 30 teams take part. Six groups of five each play four group games. The six group winners advance, along with the best second-place team in each conference. These games also count toward the regular-season record.How to watch Sixers vs. Knicks NBA Cup?Prime Video has the game exclusively. There is no national TV broadcast, so a subscription or access to the service is the only way to see it live.Radio listeners have two options. The Sixers’ flagship station, 97.5 The Fanatic, carries the game in Philadelphia. The SiriusXM app also has live play-by-play nationwide, and in a car, channel 83 has the Sixers broadcast and channel 86 has the Knicks call.Philadelphia has a quick turnaround after this one. The Sixers play at the Hornets on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 6 p.m. ET. Then comes a home game against the Bulls on Nov. 2, a trip to Detroit on Nov. 4 and a Cup game at Cleveland on Nov. 6.Sixers vs. Knicks: Date, time, and venueDate: Friday, Oct. 30Time: 7:30 p.m. ETVenue: Xfinity Mobile Arena, PhiladelphiaStreaming: Prime VideoThe Sixers will wear their red Statement Edition uniforms. The Knicks will be in the white Association Edition.This is the first of four group games for Philadelphia. The rest of the Cup slate has the Sixers at Cleveland on Nov. 6 at 7:30 p.m., home against Miami on Nov. 25 at 5 p.m. and at Indiana on Nov. 27 at 7:30 p.m. The Cup final is set for Dec. 11 at Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis.Sixers vs. Knicks: Injury ReportThe Sixers have a long list, and Brown is the name to check before tip-off.Philadelphia 76ersAriel Hukporti (right Achilles tear): outDominick Barlow (low back stress reaction): outTacko Fall (left quadriceps strain): outJabari Walker (left knee tendinopathy): outJaylen Brown (left knee soreness): questionableNew York KnicksJose Alvarado (left ankle sprain): outBrown is the Sixers’ best scorer so far, and New York’s wing depth makes him a key piece in this matchup. articles.title: Knicks' Jalen Brunson Named Athlete of the Year by Philadelphia Sports Writers Association
articles.summary: New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson was named the Philadelphia Sports Writers Association's Professional Athlete of the Year for 2026 on Friday.
articles.body:
New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson was named the Philadelphia Sports Writers Association's Professional Athlete of the Year for 2026 on Friday.

Brunson, who is from New Brunswick, New Jersey, and attended college at Villanova University in Philadelphia, was named NBA Finals MVP last season after leading the Knicks to their first championship since 1973.

Ironically, the Philadelphia 76ers figure to be among the stiffest competition for Brunson and the Knicks this season after adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown during the offseason.

Brunson will officially be honored by the PSWA on Jan. 11, 2027, at the 122nd annual PSWA Awards Banquet.

articles.title: Grizzlies rookie Cameron Boozer becomes second-youngest player in NBA history to record triple-double
articles.summary: The teenage phenom might make it look awfully bright in Memphis, sooner rather than later.
articles.body:
Heading into the Memphis Grizzlies' matchup with the Portland Trail Blazers on Thursday, the primary focus was the past — namely, the Grizzlies' first meeting with former franchise superstar Ja Morant, after trading the one-time cornerstone point guard to Portland over the summer. Coming out of the contest, though, the conversation centered on the future — and on the teenage phenom who might make it look awfully bright in Memphis, sooner rather than later.

The book on Cameron Boozer coming out of Duke was that he was a high-floor player who could do a little bit of everything well — someone who might not have quite the superstar ceiling of prospective dominant wing scorers like AJ Dybantsa and Darryn Peterson, but who seemed likely to walk into the NBA as someone capable of contributing to winning right away. He'd shown that through the season's first four games, playing a strong all-around floor game in starter's minutes at the power forward position for a pleasant surprise of a Grizzlies team that won its first four games; Memphis has turned the ball over less, grabbed a higher share of available offensive and defensive rebounds, and sent opponents to the foul line less frequently with Boozer on the floor .

But even though Memphis was winning his minutes, Boozer had come out of the chute struggling with his shot, going just 11-for-35 from inside the 3-point arc and 7-for-26 beyond it in those first four games — a difficult acclimation to the highest level of the game.

"I would just say I felt a little bit out of rhythm," Boozer said of his play to start the season. "Obviously, coming away with the win is the biggest thing. For me, I was impacting winning in all those games, but I wanted to play better."

Boozer was brilliant in Portland, going 6-for-10 from the field and 4-for-5 from 3-point land en route to 18 points in the Grizzlies' 124-103 win over the previously undefeated Blazers. The rookie added 12 rebounds and 12 assists in just 28 minutes of work, notching the first triple-double of his NBA career in just his fifth professional game.

"It took him long enough," Grizzlies coach Tuomas Iisalo joked .

At 19 years and 103 days old, Boozer is the second-youngest player in NBA history to put up a triple-double , just behind Josh Giddey, who did so at 19 years and 84 days as a rookie with the Oklahoma City Thunder in 2022. Boozer is also just the second player ever to notch a triple-double before ever actually losing an NBA game, according to Opta , joining Oscar Robertson, who did it in his first ever NBA contest. (Naturally.)

Boozer showcased the breadth of his skillset in Thursday's win, from the ability to face up and drive on defenders from the perimeter to his comfort with initiating offense from up top and acting as a playmaking hub in the middle of the floor against zone defenses. He showed soft touch on high-low lobs to his frontcourt partners, and a smooth shooting stroke as he knocked down spot-up jumpers; he even confidently stepped into triples when Portland's bigs hung back on him, whether retreating to wall off against the drive or ducking under the screen when Boozer handled the ball in an inverted pick-and-roll.

Of course, the fact that Boozer can run inverted pick-and-rolls with the Grizzlies' guards screening is evidence of perhaps the most advanced part of his game: his ability to facilitate, process the game at lightning speed, and deliver the ball wherever it should go on a given possession.

He can work either end of the two-man game, showing a capacity to quickly read the floor in the short roll and deliver skip passes to waiting shooters. He can work with his back to the basket, posting up smaller defenders, mapping the floor, drawing help and instantly kicking it to an open man on the weak side. When he clears the defensive glass, he immediately looks up the floor and flings hit-ahead outlet passes that gets the Grizzlies into early offense in transition.

And he does it all fast . Of the 35 players who are averaging at least 65 touches per game, Boozer has the lowest average time per touch , holding onto the ball for just 2.14 seconds before moving it — nearly a half-second faster than Nikola Jokić, long the measuring stick for quick decision-making and fluid offensive distribution.

That combination of skills has made Boozer a plus frontcourt playmaker from the second he stepped onto an NBA court. Boozer has notched the assist on 26.5% of the Grizzlies' baskets during his time on the floor this season. The only power forward/center types to play at least 100 minutes this season with a higher assist rate than Boozer's are Jokić, Jayson Tatum, Alperen Şengün, Draymond Green, Domantas Sabonis, Giannis Antetokounmpo and Julius Randle — all multi-time All-Star and All-NBA forwards.

Being that good at delivering the ball this young is … well, it's an anomaly. No 19-year-old big man has ever posted an assist rate above 20% for a full season . The only teens above 6-foot-8 who've finished north of 25%? Luka Dončić and LeBron James.

After Thursday's win, Boozer is averaging 15.8 points, 10.8 rebounds and 6.2 assists per game. No rookie has ever averaged 15-10-5 for a full season . Only 24 players of any age ever have . Ten of them are already in the Hall of Fame ; the list of those who aren't includes three active MVPs (Jokić, Antetokounmpo, Joel Embiid), a fourth who just retired (Russell Westbrook), and 10 other multi-time All-Star and/or All-NBA selections.

That is obviously very lofty company for any player, let alone one who's played all of five NBA games. But when you watch the impact that Boozer has already shown himself capable of making, and the way it all came together on Thursday — and then you remember that he won't even be able to buy a beer for two more years — you start wondering whether Boozer might not be able to raise a hell of a lot more than just the Grizzlies' floor .

"He's as complete of a player as I've seen and as mature of a rookie as I've seen in the league, too," Grizzlies point guard Ty Jerome, who has turned quite a few heads himself in the season's opening week, told reporters . "There's nothing he can't do on the basketball court."

articles.title: Jayson Tatum Teases NBA MVP Aspirations in New Video After Celtics' Jaylen Brown Trade
articles.summary: Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum has his sights set on potentially winning the NBA MVP Award for the first time in his career.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum has his sights set on potentially winning the NBA MVP Award for the first time in his career.

In an interview released this week with Hoop Genius, Tatum was asked about his MVP hopes, and the six-time All-Star responded by saying, "You know what? It's like, why not me? So, this the year."

Tatum, 28, has been among the NBA's best players for much of his career, dating back to when the Celtics selected him third overall in the 2017 NBA draft.

Prior to last season, which saw him limited to just 16 games while recovering from a torn Achilles, Tatum had earned six consecutive All-Star nods and four consecutive All-NBA First Team selections.

The former Duke standout also had a pair of fourth-place finishes and a pair of sixth-place finishes in the NBA MVP voting during that stretch.

All of that, as well as winning the NBA championship in 2024, was done alongside a fellow star in Jaylen Brown.

However, Brown is no longer in the mix, as the Celtics traded him to the Philadelphia 76ers during the offseason in exchange for Paul George and draft picks.

With Tatum as the unquestioned go-to guy, he is averaging 28.0 points, 8.0 assists, 6.3 rebounds, 1.8 three-pointers made and 1.0 steal per game through four contests for the 3-1 Celtics so far this season.

His current scoring average would be the second-highest of his career over the course of a full season, while his 8.0 assists per game are significantly more than his previous career high of 6.0.

Tatum very well may be in the mix for MVP by the end of the season, but he will face some stiff competition in the form of Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokić, Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Dončić and San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama.

His MVP candidacy also figures to hinge on where the Celtics finish in a competitive Eastern Conference that will see them jockeying for position with the 76ers, New York Knicks and Detroit Pistons, among others.

articles.standfirst: La rotación de los blancos se ha quedado en sólo 12 jugadores para los próximos encuentros y ya se plantean hacer fichajes
articles.summary: La rotación de los blancos se ha quedado en sólo 12 jugadores para los próximos encuentros y ya se plantean hacer fichajes
articles.body: Las lesiones que ha sufrido el Real Madrid en los últimos encuentros le van a hacer mirar al mercado en busca de refuerzos. Ya estuvo cerca de hacer una incorporación para suplir la baja de Gabriel Deck y ahora, con más motivo. Un club como el blanco siempre está abierto a hacer movimientos, pero después de los últimos acontecimientos parece casi obligado a ello porque la rotación se le ha quedado corta de repente. Las lesiones de Jantunen (rotura completa de la fascia plantar del pie izquierdo) y Maledon (esguince en la rodilla derecha) se suman a las que padecen Usman Garuba, que va a perderse casi la totalidad de la temporada; el mencionado Deck, que estará unos cuatro meses de baja tras ser operado de un hombro; y Nick Smith Jr., que también arrastra problemas en la fascia plantar. Eso reduce la plantilla drásticamente de 17 jugadores a sólo 12 de cara a los próximos encuentros. Y de los disponibles, Max Shulga y Olivier Sarr van despacio en cuanto a su adaptación al baloncesto europeo y el capitán Sergio Llull sólo han tenido hasta ahora minutos en la Liga Endesa. Este jueves entró en la convocatoria frente al Fenerbahce, pero no llegó a jugar y sigue sin estrenarse esta temporada en la máxima competición continental. Sólo el lesionado Garuba y él no han disfrutado de minutos en Europa. Con nueve encuentros en noviembre y 11 en diciembre, empezando por el de este domingo ante el Recoletas Salud San Pablo Burgos y siguiendo por el del próximo miércoles ante el Panathinaikos, el calendario no da un respiro. A quienes respete la salud, tendrán que asumir más minutos con el consiguiente riesgo. En esa situación, los blancos estarían ya mirando el mercado en busca de algún refuerzo no sólo para ayudar de forma inmediata sino para aliviar la carga física de algunas piezas clave. Uno de los primeros nombres que han aparecido es el de Eli John Ndiaye. Después de que el Madrid igualara la oferta del Valencia Basket en el tanteo el pasado verano, el canterano está cedido en el Asisa Joventut, pero puede ser repescado después del 15 de noviembre si hubiera problema de cupos en las competiciones ACB. Ahora, sin contar al lesionado Usman Garuba, dispone de cinco: Llull, Alberto Abalde, Edy Tavares, Jaime Pradilla y Shulga, que hasta hace poco parecía que podía salir cedido, aunque todo ha cambiado tras las últimas lesiones. Toda mano es bienvenida.

articles.title: Radicevic, fichaje temporal para el Asisa Joventut
articles.standfirst: El base serbio firma por dos meses ante la baja de Lude Hakanson
articles.summary: El base serbio firma por dos meses ante la baja de Lude Hakanson
articles.body: El base serbio Nikola Radicevic ha firmado un contrato de dos meses con el Asisa Joventut, según ha anunciado este viernes el conjunto catalán, que de este modo reforzará el juego exterior ante la baja del sueco Lude Hakanson. Radicevic, de 32 años y 1,97 metros, destaca por su físico, lectura de juego y habilidad en el bloqueo directo, e inició su formación en el Partizan de Belgrado antes de recalar por primera vez en España en 2012, en las filas del Cajasol de Sevilla, donde progresó hasta consolidarse en el primer equipo bajo las órdenes del entrenador Aíto García Reneses. El base de Cacak (Serbia) cuenta con una amplia trayectoria en el baloncesto europeo y, especialmente, en la Liga Endesa, con 183 partidos repartidos en once temporadas en cinco equipos distintos: Sevilla (Cajasol primero, después Baloncesto Sevilla y Betis), Gran Canaria, UCAM Murcia, Surne Bilbao Basket y MoraBanc Andorra. El Joventut recurre a este fichaje por la baja de Hakanson, que se recupera de una lesión en el tobillo izquierdo para la que el club verdinegro no ha especificado el tiempo previsto de baja. El sueco era un hombre importante en la rotación del técnico Dani Miret para dar descanso a los dos directores de juego principales del equipo, los veteranos Nico Laprovittola y Ricky Rubio. Además, la Penya también cuenta actualmente con la baja del estadounidense Boogie Ellis, lesionado en el aductor de la pierna derecha, cuyo regreso a las pistas podría producirse ya la semana que viene.

articles.title: Trey Murphy III, Herb Jones Linked as Potential Thunder Trade Targets in New NBA Rumors
articles.summary: As the Oklahoma City Thunder search for reinforcements with Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace expected to potentially miss the remainder of the 2026-27 NBA regular season, two members of the New Orleans Pelicans could emerge as trade targets for Sam Presti.
articles.body:
As the Oklahoma City Thunder search for reinforcements with Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace expected to potentially miss the remainder of the 2026-27 NBA regular season, two members of the New Orleans Pelicans could emerge as trade targets for Sam Presti.

Per ESPN's Tim MacMahon , multiple league executives cited Trey Murphy III or Herb Jones as potential trade targets for the Thunder.

One potential issue, as MacMahon pointed out, is New Orleans has sought "multiple first-round picks" for Murphy in the past and Presti is not one to trade part with those kinds of assets.

"That's not who they are," one Eastern Conference executive told MacMahon about the idea of Oklahoma City potentially trading first-round picks. "I think they'd rather play their young guys and see what they have."

In the same ESPN report, Brian Windhorst quoted a Western Conference executive who thinks Jones could be difficult to trade because of the three-year, $67.6 million extension New Orleans gave him in July 2025 that kicks in next season.

"That is a negative value contract to us," the exec said. "[New Orleans] would have some trouble trading him for anything close to what they'd asked for him in the past."

One under-the-radar trade option that could emerge for the Thunder is Sacramento Kings guard Nique Clifford, per MacMahon.

Coincidentally, Clifford was originally drafted by Oklahoma City with the No. 24 pick in 2025. He was flipped to the Kings for a 2027 protected first-round pick that originally belonged to the San Antonio Spurs.

After averaging 25.1 minutes per game in 78 appearances as a rookie last season, Clifford has not been a factor in the Kings' rotation through their first five games this season. He has played a total of 28 minutes in four appearances.

Both Williams (fractured fibula, dislocated ankle) and Wallace (torn labrum) required surgery for injuries suffered in a win over the Los Angeles Clippers on Oct. 25. The Thunder stopped short of officially ruling them out for the season, but they are going to be out indefinitely.

Oklahoma City have eight first-round picks between 2027 to '33 that could be used to build a trade.

Presti hasn't made a trade giving up multiple first-round picks since June 2022 when he acquired the No. 11 overall pick in that draft (used to select Ousmane Dieng) from the New York Knicks for a package that included three protected picks in the 2023 draft.

Another problem for the Thunder when it comes to acquiring a player like either Murphy or Jones is financial in nature. They traded away Isaiah Joe, Lu Dort and Aaron Wiggins over the summer in part to stay below the second apron this season.

With Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's extension kicking in next season, raising his salary to a projected $61 million, the Thunder are already set to be almost $26 million over the projected second apron in 2027-28. Murphy is owed $29 million next season.

The Thunder staying out of the second apron this year does allow Presti some flexibility with trades, but it would seem unlikely anything happens soon as they look to see how their current talent pool plays without Williams and Wallace.

articles.title: Warriors' Yaxel Lendeborg Says He Won't Take Media Training, 'Going to Stay True to Myself'
articles.summary: Having already garnered as much attention for things he says as his play on the court, Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has no intention of changing his approach.
articles.body:
Having already garnered as much attention for things he says as his play on the court, Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has no intention of changing his approach.

Speaking to Luca Evans of the San Francisco Chronicle , Lendeborg explained he is "going to stay true to myself" when asked about potentially taking media training:

"I'm not doing that, man. I'm going to stay true to myself, and be honest. I've seen plenty of interviews where people are talking and it's like, 'Man, I don't want to watch this,' you know what I mean? And it's not like I'm click-baiting or click-farming or whatever the heck people are saying. But it's like, that's honestly how I feel," Lendeborg continued. "And I'm not gonna lie about it. I've never been a liar. So, just tell the truth."

Insider Explains Yaxel vs. Kuminga Opportunity

One of the biggest stories of the NBA season thus far came on opening night after the Wariors lost to the Los Angeles Lakers, when Lendeborg called out Luka Dončić for frequently complaining to the officials.

There have been moments since then that have endeared Lendeborg to fans. During a postgame interview on NBA Showtime after the Warriors' win over the Denver Nuggets on Monday, Lendeborg asked studio analysts and NBA legends Carmelo Anthony, Vince Carter and Tracy McGrady if they had any advice for him early in his career.

Warriors head coach Steve Kerr didn't take issue with Lendeborg's comments about Dončić, though he did joke about not fouling the Lakers star next time.

The discussion around Lendeborg's knack for commentary isn't doing anything to negatively impact his play. He's averaging 22.6 points, 9.2 rebounds and 4.0 assists per game in five starts.

Lendeborg has put up at least 26 points and nine rebounds in three straight games. The Warriors have won their last two games after an 0-3 start.

Lendeborg and the Warriors will get their second look at Doncic and the Lakers on Friday night at 10 p.m. ET.

The much-maligned statue of Hall of Famer Dwyane Wade outside the Miami Heat's Kaseya Center received some significant improvements this week.

articles.body:
Dwyane Wade's statue outside of the Kaseya Center in Miami looks a little bit different now two years after it was officially unveiled.

The former Miami Heat star was honored with the 8-foot bronze statue which immortalized the moment on March 9, 2009, when Wade hit a game-winning shot in a double-overtime matchup with the Chicago Bulls , after which he stood on the scorer's table and declared: " This is my house! "

But the statue depicting the basketball Hall of Famer didn't appear to resemble that of Wade , who played 15 years with the franchise.

Wade brushed off the jokes and memes at the time, but the noise was loud enough that the team decided to make an adjustment and have a new head created.

On Substack , Wade wrote, "If people don't feel that connection when they look at the face, why wouldn't we try to make it better?" After discussions with the team, all parties agreed to the change.

It gave us a chance to make sure the face better connects with the person and the emotion the statue is meant to represent. This isn't about erasing the work that was already done or disrespecting the artists who put their time and talent into creating it. It's about being willing to listen. It's about recognizing when something carries meaning for more people than just yourself and being open enough to revisit it. This is the first statue ever to stand in front of that arena. That means something to me, but it also means something to the city. Miami deserves to feel proud of it. The 305 deserves to look at that statue and feel the same energy it felt that night. articles.title: Dan Hurley, UConn Reportedly Agree to Contract Extension Ahead of 2026-27 CBB Season
articles.summary: Three days away from Connecticut's first game of the 2026-27 college basketball season, head coach Dan Hurley has agreed to a contract extension.
articles.body:
Three days away from Connecticut's first game of the 2026-27 college basketball season, head coach Dan Hurley has agreed to a contract extension.

Per Jon Rothstein of CBS Sports and 247Sports, Hurley will sign a new deal that keeps him under contract with the Huskies through the 2031-32 season.

Financial details of the agreement are unknown, but Rothstein noted it will keep Hurley among the highest-paid coaches in college basketball.

Hurley was under contract through the 2029-30 season after signing a six-year, $50 million deal in July 2024. That agreement came about following his talks with the Los Angeles Lakers about their head-coaching position.

Kansas' Bill Self was the only men's college basketball head coach who made more than Hurley's $8.025 million base salary during the 2025-26 season. His deal also had the highest buyout at $34.8 million as of April 1.

If Hurley coaches for the entirety of his new deal, he will have spent 14 consecutive seasons at UConn. Jim Calhoun (27 seasons) and Hugh Greer (17 seasons) would be the only head coaches with a longer tenure at the university.

Hurley already ranks third in Huskies history with 199 victories through his first eight seasons. He has won at least 31 games three times in the last four seasons with three Final Four appearances and two national titles during that span.

Connecticut is entering the 2026-27 season ranked No. 4 in the Associated Press Top 25 preseason poll. It's the fourth consecutive year the Huskies have started a season ranked sixth or better.

Hurley and the Huskies will tipoff the regular season on Monday when they take on Gardner-Webb at PeoplesBank Arena in Hartford.

articles.title: Thunder Reportedly to Sign Former NBA Lottery Pick After Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace Injuries
articles.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder are reportedly planning to sign free agent guard Ochai Agbaji, per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder are reportedly planning to sign free agent guard Ochai Agbaji, per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.

Agbaji, the 14th pick in the 2022 NBA draft, has played for the Utah Jazz, Toronto Raptors and Brooklyn Nets over a four-year career.

The former Kansas star joined the Knicks on an Exhibit 9 contract (one-year training camp deal) in September but got waived on Oct. 16.

The Thunder signed Agbaji after injuries to forward Jalen Williams (fractured left fibula and dislocated ankle) and guard Cason Wallace (torn labrum in left shoulder).

Agbaji has played 263 games (108 starts) over his four seasons, averaging 7.2 points on 44.8 percent shooting (33.9 percent from three) and 2.7 rebounds per game.

The Cleveland Cavaliers initially selected Agbaji in the draft but traded him to the Utah Jazz amid the blockbuster Donovan Mitchell deal.

He played a season-and-a-half with Utah before the Jazz dealt him to Toronto. Agbaji then went to the Nets in Feb. 2026 in a three-team deal that also included the Los Angeles Clippers.

Agbaji didn't see much preseason playing time with the Knicks, suiting up for 29 minutes over three games.

Now Agbaji gets a chance with the Thunder, who also recently signed Micah Peavy to a two-way contract.

OKC started the season 4-0 before falling at the Dallas Mavericks on Wednesday. The Thunder will now continue their road trip and play the 5-0 Houston Rockets on Saturday.

articles.title: Kentucky Appeals Judge Denies NCAA Bid to Block 30 Athletes from Playing as Hoops Season Draws Near
articles.summary: The NCAA was denied emergency relief by a Kentucky Court of Appeals judge Friday, leaving eligible a host of college athletes as the basketball season is about to begin until a panel of three judges can consider the governing body's request for relief.
articles.body:
The NCAA was denied emergency relief by a Kentucky Court of Appeals judge Friday, leaving eligible a host of college athletes as the basketball season is about to begin until a panel of three judges can consider the governing body's request for relief.

The 30 athletes involved, including Missouri basketball player Mark Mitchell and LSU's Skyy Clark, received a temporary injunction Oct. 16 to compete while the NCAA appealed a ruling that allowed members of the 2022 high school graduating class to play a final season in their respective sports under the NCA's new five-for-five model.

Kentucky judge Sara Walter Combs wrote in her decision that the NCAA failed to prove that the injunction created "imminent, ruinous and incalculable injury," and that it serves no purpose "to flip-flop repeatedly as our courts work through the underlying issues."

Along with allowing the basketball players involved in the case to begin their seasons next week, the ruling allows football players Alex Afari Jr. of Kentucky, Texas Tech quarterback Thomas Castellanos and Louisville football players Jabari Mack and Kalib Perry — all of whom are also involved in the litigation — to continue to compete while the case plays out.

Multiple lawsuits filed in several states have focused on the NCAA's new eligibility model due to be implemented next fall. It allows athletes five years of eligibility beginning when an athlete turns 19 or graduates from high school, whichever is earliest.

But the implementation excluded athletes who began college careers during the 2022-23 season and completed four years. And those athletes, including some who have played for professional teams, are now suing to play their fifth season in college.

The ruling in Kentucky came one day after the Ohio Supreme Court kept in place a ruling from earlier this month allowing two dozen players involved in an eligibility case there to remain available for their teams. The lead plaintiff is Filip Borovicanin of Xavier, which opens its season Monday, while other basketball players involved include Gonzaga's Javon Bennett and MJ Collins of Cincinnati.

The NCAA legal office sent a memo to its members late Thursday saying it was "deeply disappointed" by the outcome in Ohio.

"Every minute played by an ineligible player is an opportunity deprived to an eligible student-athlete — sometimes in the pinnacle events of a season," the NCAA's letter said. "And it provides a significant competitive advantage to schools rostering experienced players who exhausted their eligibility."

articles.title: 76ers' Dean Wade Jokes About LeBron James Handshake After Viral Video, 'I Can't Do This Stuff'
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers forward Dean Wade discussed the simplistic nature of the handshake he shared with teammate LeBron James prior to the team's loss to the Detroit Pitons on Sunday.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers forward Dean Wade discussed the simplistic nature of the handshake he shared with teammate LeBron James prior to the team's loss to the Detroit Pitons on Sunday.

After doing extravagant handshakes with Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, James shared a more traditional one with Wade, which turned the video into a viral sensation:

Speaking to reporters this week about the interaction, Wade said, "I just have the simple, 'Hire me' handshake. I try to stay out of it because I can't do this stuff."

Alex Coffey of the Philadelphia Inquirer later clarified that Wade's comment was made "in jest."

Per Coffey , specialized handshakes are something LeBron has done for the entirety of his career, including his stints with the Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat and Los Angeles Lakers.

In addition to having a different handshake for every teammate, he also has greetings for "coaches, team attendants, locker room managers and photographers."

James and Wade are both newcomers to the Sixers this season, although LeBron's arrival was undoubtedly met with more fanfare.

It was a busy offseason in Philly with the signing of James and trade acquisition of Brown from the Boston Celtics, which are moves that instantly made the 76ers serious championship contenders.

Through five games, the Sixers are tied with the Pistons for the best record in the East at 4-1, solidifying their status as one of the teams to beat.

If that holds true, LeBron and his teammates could be sharing handshakes into June as part of a lengthy playoff run.

articles.title: Ja Morant Injured, Latest Updates on Hamstring Strain and Timeline to Return to Blazers
articles.summary: The Portland Trail Blazers announced Friday that guard Ja Morant is expected to miss at least a month of action.
articles.body:
The Portland Trail Blazers announced Friday that guard Ja Morant is expected to miss at least a month of action.

The team noted that Morant will be re-evaluated in four weeks after leaving Thursday's loss to the Memphis Grizzlies with what was later determined to be a Grade 2 left hamstring strain.

Portland acquired Morant from the Grizzlies this past offseason in exchange for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray.

Morant, who was a two-time All-Star and NBA Rookie of the Year during his seven seasons with the Grizzlies, was a significant part of the Blazers' backcourt rotation through four games this season.

In 25.8 minutes per game, the 27-year-old veteran is averaging 15.8 points, 5.5 assists, 2.5 rebounds, 1.5 three-pointers made and 1.0 steal per contest, while shooting 54.2 percent from the field and 42.9 percent from beyond the arc.

Morant had a hand in the Blazers getting off to a 3-0 start prior to Thursday's loss to the Grizzlies, who improved to an NBA-best 5-0 with their victory.

While losing Morant for an extended period of time is far from ideal, the Blazers do at least have the benefit of a ton of depth at the guard position.

Along with Morant, Portland has veterans Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday on the roster, plus 2023 No. 3 overall draft pick Scoot Henderson.

All of them figure to see a bump in playing time and importance while Morant is out, plus leading scorer Deni Avdija will continue to lead the way offensively.

Portland will be back in action Saturday when it goes on the road to face the Utah Jazz.

articles.title: Return of the Mac
articles.summary: SYRACUSE, N.Y. — Rare is the top-level college athlete who actually sets a goal to, someday, be a top-level college coach. Prove it wrong. Find the kid who g...
articles.body:
SYRACUSE, N.Y. — Rare is the top-level college athlete who actually sets a goal to, someday, be a top-level college coach.

Prove it wrong. Find the kid who grew up dribbling a basketball for hours around his driveway, who wouldn't leave the gym until he drained 100 3-pointers, whose ultimate goal was to be his generation's Phil Jackson, not its Michael Jordan. You sure wouldn't have found him in the early 2000s in Scranton.

Back when legendary Syracuse men's basketball coach Jim Boeheim made the two-hour trek south on Interstate 81 to recruit him, Gerry McNamara never envisioned a day when Boeheim's program would be his, because the Scranton hoops icon never considered coaching as an ambition. The greats rarely do.

"I never envisioned being a coach. I always envisioned playing in the NBA," McNamara said. "(Coaching) is something I didn't envision, but immediately, I knew it was something I could love from the first workout I did with the guards back in 2009. I knew that this was going to be something I could dive fully into."

On Monday night, McNamara will be patrolling the sidelines for the first time in a game that matters as Syracuse's head coach when the Orange host the University of New Haven in the regular season opener at the JHA Wireless Dome. It will mark a long-awaited homecoming to a program he helped to its lone national championship in 2003, willed to an epic Big East title in 2006, aided as an assistant coach to nine NCAA tournament appearances and two Final Fours — and is also pining for a return to that glory.

Nobody knows better than McNamara that the one NCAA tournament game tiny Siena University played in during his two seasons as head coach there is one more than the once-mighty Orange have played in over the last five years.

Back in the arena with which he became synonymous, in a role most everyone there but him figured he'd be ideal to assume.

Back to prove an ever-changing landscape in collegiate athletics is no match for ideals that have always mattered most to him.

Back to pursue a return to glory, in a place longing for it.

There is no better place to gauge the excitement of McNamara's Syracuse return than on the team's website.

There, atop a list of links that will take you to the season schedule, statistics, or anything about the program's extensive list of All-Americans that range from Dave Bing to Carmelo Anthony, you'll find a link that will take you to a page dedicated solely to McNamara.

"Welcome Home," the headline blares, in oversized capital letters. Cleverly, Syracuse is calling this season the beginning of the program's "McNamERA."

He was only gone two seasons, off to guide Siena after Syracuse's athletic administrators elected to replace the iconic Boeheim as head coach with Adrian Autry in 2023. But the road to becoming the Orange's head coach seemed somewhat long for McNamara.

At the beginning, he put it off for a while, floating around professional leagues in Eastern Europe and even the NBA's G-League, scrapping for an NBA opportunity that never did come his way. Even as he longed for a return home, it took him two weeks in the spring of 2009 to consider Boeheim's offer to join his staff as a graduate assistant coach working with the team's guards.

"(Boeheim) said, "I think it's something you're probably not looking for, but I think it's also something you'll be good at," McNamara recalled.

McNamara made the painful decision to end his playing days and pursue a different basketball destiny.

So, with each bit of instruction, each bit of through-the-battles wisdom, he provided stars like young point guard Scoop Jardine and former teammate Andy Rautins, the Orange's starting shooting guard in 2009, McNamara learned something about his new role.

"I had the attention of the guys I was working with," McNamara said. "These guys knew exactly who I was and saw the success. Andy Rautins, he became my guy, one of my best friends to this day. But working with him every day, just firing hundreds of passes at him and him just shooting, knowing I was a part of the success of anything I could do for this kid, because I knew he was going to be ready on game night, which he always was. It was just kind of the same rewarding feeling as if I went out there and made the play myself. I helped the guy prepare to go do it himself. It's the same reward (as playing), in a completely different way."

He always believed coaching basketball couldn't exactly match the feeling of playing it.

But coaching sure felt an awful lot like competing. And, really, competition has always been the driving force in his athletic life.

McNamara was hooked, and he attacked his new passion with the same ferocity he mustered during the PIAA playoffs at Bishop Hannan, or the Big Dance with the Orange.

He went from graduate assistant to full-time assistant in two seasons under Boeheim's tutelage. Autry made him Syracuse's associate head coach in 2023, when he took over as head coach. During the time in between, McNamara became one of the most consistent recruiters along the east coast, dedicated to building personal relationships in an age of college basketball where so many programs rely on transactional ones.

In his debut season at Syracuse, McNamara finds himself in a rare situation. Technically, he's a newcomer, barely more than 200 days on the job, but his fingerprints already are all over the Orange roster.

White, a highly regarded forward who boasted offers from some of the top college programs in the nation coming out of high school, committed to Syracuse after the then-assistant McNamara spoke to him on a recruiting visit. With lucrative offers to make a switch to another program through the NCAA's transfer portal after Autry's firing, White elected to stay with the Orange, primarily because they hired the guy he wanted to play for all along.

"He," White raved of McNamara, "is the ultimate human being."

It's a rare thing to hear from college athletes these days.

Prospects like White typically don't look for those kinds of relationships when they're searching for a school to play at, because they rules say they don't have to; Long gone are the days when a prospective student-athlete, at 18 years old, essentially made a four-year decision coming out of prep school. The transfer portal allows them to pursue any opportunity available, and new Name, Image and Likeness rules that can lead to the better transfers earning upwards of $1 million to skip town essentially makes them no different than NBA free agents.

But for as much as his reputation as a player intrigues his charges, it is McNamara's charm away from the court that has always stood out to players.

Scrappy freshman point guard Ryan Moesch, who committed to McNamara at Siena, followed McNamara to Syracuse not because their games were similar, but because he found his chosen coach to be "a real dude." Sophomore forward Frances Folefac played for McNamara as a freshman at Siena, then tagged along to Syracuse because McNamara "treats me as family."

There may not be a better example of McNamara's emphasis on building relationship-driven programs than Gavin Doty.

The 6-foot-5 junior who starred for Siena in its near upset of top-seeded Duke in the first round of the NCAA Tournament in March was a McNamara favorite long before his recruiting process began.

Doty grew up in Fulton, N.Y., in the shadow of Lake Ontario and a 30-minute drive away from the Syracuse camps he used to frequent as a youngster. That is where he caught McNamara's eye, and where the baby-faced sharpshooter first dreamt of playing college ball.

The first college visit he made was to McNamara at Siena. He had five others lined up after that.

He liked Siena a lot. But he loved McNamara, his family-first viewpoints, his emphasis on belief, his passion for winning. So when McNamara asked what it would take to convince him to sign on with his Saints. That's when Doty smiled, and surprised McNamara — and his own parents, for that matter — with the news that he'd be canceling his other five visits.

"I've never heard anybody say anything bad about G-Mac, in terms of his character and how he treats people, how passionate he is and how he was as a player," Doty said. "Being around him is amazing. He makes you want to run through a brick wall for him. He'll say something before a game, or even a practice, and you can feel his spirit. You can feel his passion, especially about this place."

He has gone through successes and frustrations. He has had plans foiled, and balked at different ones. He began his career in a world of collegiate athletics that seems almost backward compared to the one that exists now and has embraced the personal changes in approach that had to come with it.

But, in a situation where coaches have to deal as much with agents now as they do with parents, high school coaches and, sometimes, the players themselves, there is one ideal from which Gerry McNamara has no plans to deviate.

Each day, he and members of his staff spend an hour outside of practices or games working with players on personal development. That might be basketball-related. It might be education-based. Whatever it is, though, the intention is clear: Build successful people, not just winning rosters.

"Ultimately, we come in here as competitors, and we need to win the day," White said. "But as a man, there are days you don't win. There are times you don't come out on top. Those are the days when coach pulls you aside and says, 'You did this wrong and this wrong, but I can see you want to get better here, and I know you can get better there.' It's just little things like that with him.

"What that tells me is, I know he's watching me. I know he believes in my game. We commit to these coaches with a dream, and this coach, he believes in my dream too."

In essence, Gerry McNamara has always been about dreams. He accomplished his fair share as a player, for sure.

This week, he officially sets sail on a different era of them.

If he can eventually achieve the goal of getting Syracuse back to national prominence, and that midcourt celebration after the national championship game he knows so well, it will further emblaze his legend both in upstate New York and back in Scranton. But he knows, just as well, that pretty much everybody who is hired to do the job he has ends up getting thanked for his efforts and urged on his way.

Those relationships, then, better lead to a winning culture, he said.

"It's what we're judged on," McNamara conceded. "But I won't sacrifice the development piece. I said it when I first got the Siena job: We're going to recruit high-character kids, and we're going to develop them. I'm not going to change that model. We hope all the work we put in with them ultimately leads to that gameday moment where it's no longer about development. Now you've got to perform."

Nobody did that better at Syracuse as a player than McNamara, when he was pursuing his own dream. He returns to the sidelines Monday pushing to live another one.
authors: Donnie Collins, The Times-Tribune, Scranton, Pa.

articles.title: Memphis basketball may go legal route if Nemanja Popović appeal denied, Penny Hardaway says
articles.summary: Memphis basketball coach Penny Hardaway did not rule out the possibility of seeking legal relief in the Nemanja Popović eligibility saga.
articles.body:
Memphis basketball coach Penny Hardaway did not rule out the possibility of seeking legal relief in the Nemanja Popović eligibility saga if the program's appeal of the NCAA's decision is denied.

"I think we will have other options if the appeal isn't granted to keep fighting it until we can't fight it anymore," Hardaway told reporters Oct. 30. "We hope the appeal goes through, but yeah, we're looking for other options as well."

The NCAA deemed the Tigers' center eligible for the 2026-27 and 2027-28 seasons but mandated a six-game "withholding period" to be served starting with the team's regular-season opener against Iowa State (6 p.m., Nov. 2, FS1). The issue, according to Hardaway, is the number of games Popović played during the 2022-23 season. The 24-year-old is in his first season of college basketball after playing professionally overseas since 2019.

Memphis announced it was appealing the NCAA's ruling on Oct. 26. Hardaway is hopeful the appeal will be decided before tip-off against Iowa State, but as of 1:30 p.m. CT on Oct. 30, the school had not received any update from the NCAA.

See our best photos from Memphis basketball's exhibition against Arkansas

Popović played in all three of the Tigers' preseason games, most recently scoring 16 points and grabbing six rebounds in a loss at Arkansas. Hardaway said the prospect of not having him for any amount of time is "a tough problem."

"He's like the backbone of the offense, because we go through him for a lot of the things that we run," said Hardaway. "But (the coaching staff) has done a good job with the other frontcourt guys. Obviously, they don't have the same amount of talent, but they have the same amount of will power. All we need them to do is go out and play hard, play tough. We don't know exactly which guy we're gonna go with. Probably (Maxim Logue).

"When you've got 'Pop,' you can go inside and slow the game down. When he's not out there, you can play fast. We're definitely going to play to our strengths."

Memphis point guard Jayden Reid said Popović has kept his head up as the situation has played out.

"Obviously, we need him out there, we want him out there," Reid said. "He's a big part of what we're doing this year. He has a positive attitude about it. Whoever's out there, we're going to compete. We're trying to win the game no matter who's out there."

articles.title: Ernie Johnson hopes ‘Inside The NBA’ continues long after retirement decision
articles.summary: The end of an era is finally here as the longtime host of ‘Inside The NBA,’ Ernie Johnson, announced his decision to step down from his current role. Althoug...
articles.body:
The end of an era is finally here as the longtime host of ' Inside The NBA ,' Ernie Johnson , announced his decision to step down from his current role. Although he did not officially say he was retired, he will not be involved as much and certainly won't continue to host the show. While his announcement leaves questions as to what will happen to award-winning show , Johnson is hoping it continues even after his depature.

"I have no idea, and I don't want to be blamed for ending 'Inside The NBA.' In my role, I'm stepping away from my role on there. I would hope that they could continue the show in some form," Johnson said during a recent segment with Front Office Sports. "There are plenty of great studio hosts out there who could do what I do."

Ernie Johnson also touched briefly on the potential departure of Charles Barkley from 'Inside The NBA' in saying that he doesn't know what the future holds for the NBA Hall of Famer and that he'll leave it up to Barkley to have the final word on that. Barkley has said in the past that he would retire as well when Johnson did so.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

This is the second season that 'Inside The NBA' has been broadcast on ESPN following the league's restructuring of their media rights deals. Prior to that, the show had aired on TNT Sports since 1989. Johnson joined the show in 1990 and has been in his role as host ever since.

During his tenure, alongside Barkley, Kenny Smith and later Shaquille O'Neal, the show has won 19 Sports Emmy Awards, and Johnson and Barkley have each won individual awards.

articles.title: Kings star Ben Simmons’ ‘unicorn’ declaration sparks fan reactions all over the map
articles.summary: Ben Simmons was very close to making a stunning return to the NBA after last having played in the league in the 2024-25 for the Los Angeles Clippers. However...
articles.body:
Ben Simmons was very close to making a stunning return to the NBA after last having played in the league in the 2024-25 for the Los Angeles Clippers. However, after signing a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Sacramento Kings , Simmons suffered a torn right Achilles tendon , which means he is out for the entire season.

However, after undergoing successful surgery, Simmons appears to be as confident as ever that he will eventually return to the NBA. Speaking to Andscape, the 30-year-old claimed that he was not a typical player, and described himself as a 'unicorn,' per a post on X by NBACentral.

"I'm more than capable of playing in this league," he said. "I'm built for this. I'm not a normal guy. I'm kind of like a unicorn in the sense of how I play the game. I'm not your typical player. I don't know how to put it, but I feel like I'm a lot different than most."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Fans, however, had a range of reactions to his declaration. Some, like this one , claimed that he does more talking than playing, posting alongside an image of Shaquille O'Neal laughing.

"Bro does more talking than playing," they wrote.

Another fan questioned his shooting, writing, "He's definitely different. Most basketball players can shoot."

This fan played around with the 'unicorn' declaration, writing , "Ben Simmons is a unicorn on the court. You'll never see him but people will tell fantasies about him playing."

Simmons was selected as the No. 1 pick of the 2016 draft by the Philadelphia 76ers, and after sitting out for his first season due to a foot injury, won the Rookie of the Year in the 2017-18 campaign. There is no doubt that Simmons, when fit, was a special player.

An elite guard with impressive vision, his playmaking immediately led to comparisons with some of the greatest assist-makers in the history of the league. However, it was his combination of size and versatility in defence that truly made him special. Simmons was capable of locking down the most skilful players in the league, and was also a major interior presence who could have easily become a triple-double machine.

However, consistent injuries meant that the 76ers eventually traded him to the Brooklyn Nets, and he has since failed to keep fit for a full season. Regardless, the Kings star did express confidence in his recent interview, claiming that he will do everything in his power to remain healthy and return to his best. And well, there is little doubt that every basketball fan would like to see that happen.

articles.title: FSU freshman lands on national preseason watch list
articles.summary: Florida State freshman center Marcis Ponder was named to the Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Award preseason watch list after an impressive exhibition showing.
articles.body:
Florida State Seminoles freshman center Marcis Ponder is already drawing national recognition before playing his first official college game.

Ponder has been named to the preseason watch list for the 2027 Kareem Abdul-Jabbar Award, presented annually by the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame to the top center in Division I men's college basketball. The award is part of the Hall of Fame's Starting Five honors and is named for three-time NCAA champion and Hall of Famer Kareem Abdul-Jabbar.

The recognition comes after an encouraging preseason debut for the 7-foot, 285-pound freshman.

Ponder made an immediate impression in Florida State's exhibition victory over the Auburn Tigers , finishing with 13 points, 21 rebounds and three blocks in 25 minutes. The Seminoles won 82-71, with Ponder's work on the glass standing out in his first appearance in an FSU uniform.

Head coach Luke Loucks has set an extremely high ceiling for the freshman, recently saying he believes Ponder could become one of the most productive centers in the ACC and potentially lead the country in rebounding if he stays out of foul trouble and consistently uses his size around the basket.

Those expectations are backed by Ponder's prep résumé. He arrived at Florida State as a consensus four-star prospect after averaging 20.1 points, 13.1 rebounds and 5.4 blocks per game during his final prep season. He was ranked as the No. 4 center in the 2026 class by 247Sports and earned Grind Session Defensive Player of the Year honors.

Ponder's role figures to be substantial immediately. His combination of size, rebounding and rim protection gives Loucks a true interior presence as FSU prepares to open the regular season.

Now, before that season has even begun, Ponder has already been placed among the centers to watch nationally.

articles.title: Trail Blazers' Ja Morant hit with brutal injury timeline after facing Grizzlies for first time
articles.summary: Ja Morant was traded by the Memphis Grizzlies this offseason. In his first game against his former team, he exited with an injury that looks to be a lengthy...
articles.body:
The offseason was a wild one for everyone around the league. It was filled with twists and turns, from trades to free-agent signings.

"The Grizzlies on Monday traded Ja Morant to the Trail Blazers in a move that sees Memphis start anew and gives the two-time All-Star a chance to revive his career in Portland. The Trail Blazers sent Jerami Grant and Kris Murray to the Grizzlies to complete the deal," ESPN wrote.

On Thursday night, Morant faced his former team for the first time since the trade when Portland hosted Memphis. Unfortunately, his night was cut short because of a hamstring injury.

"Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant exited his first game against his former team in the fourth quarter Thursday night because of a left hamstring injury. Morant had 14 points and three assists in 23 minutes before exiting and being ruled out of the Trail Blazers' 124-103 loss to the Memphis Grizzlies. Coach Micah Nori said postgame that Morant felt a twinge in his hamstring and that Nori hoped to have more answers Friday," ESPN wrote.

The extent of the injury was initially unknown, but on Friday afternoon, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Morant would be sidelined for at least a month.

"Portland Trail Blazers' Ja Morant has sustained a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and will miss at least four weeks, sources tell ESPN," Charania posted.

Obviously, this is a big loss for Portland, as Morant has been playing well this season. However, the good news is that the team has plenty of depth in its backcourt, meaning two-time NBA champion Jrue Holiday will likely step into the starting lineup.

It is unfortunate for this injury to happen so early in the season, especially with injuries becoming a trend around the NBA this year. Morant will now focus on getting healthy and returning to a Trail Blazers team that has gotten off to a strong start.
